correctness.rationale: Over F_2, every projective line is {x,y,x+y}, uniquely determined by two distinct points. At an even 1-WL round, any two named points give a singleton line at the next odd round and hence a singleton third point at the next even round. All unnamed y without an expression y=x+z for named x,z have identical line-colour multisets: exactly one line through each named x and uniform all-unnamed remainder. The identity T_j ∪ (T_j+T_j\{0})=T_{j+1}, with T_j all nonzero support weights ≤2^j, proves the exact induction. At the final even point-discrete round, threshold t=2^(k−1), the only possible late line collisions arise when d≥t+3, witnessed by two different t-subsets off coordinates 1,2; d≤t+2 separates already by 2k. Fewer than d named points span a proper subspace fixed pointwise by a nontrivial linear automorphism, so cannot discretize. Independent rebuilt 1-WL checks for d=2..5 returned graph-round depths 0,2,4,5. Original source checkers cover graph d=2..9 and combinatorial tests to 17 but stored logs are not proof.

The all-dimension induction is mathematical; independent direct graph enumeration was bounded to dimension five.
